transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
With Jensen Huang out as NVIDIA's CEO following revelations of an affair with a woman suspected
to be a Chinese spy, the company's chief financial officer, Collette Kress, is stepping in.
Kevin Roose, co-host of NPR's Machine Gods podcast, has more on what she'll try to do
as CEO.
Well, I think the first thing that she has to do is just to keep people calm, right?
Customers, employees, investors, people are already worried about, you know, momentum
shifting to AMD or another rival.
The second would be the money.
I mean, NVIDIA has been acting as a kind of bank for the entire AI industry.
It has deals with all of the biggest AI labs, including hundreds of billions of dollars of
commitments and circular financing deals.
And Collette Kress signed off on many of those deals, but she has to now decide whether to
keep writing the checks.
And then I just think she's going to have a lot of investigations to deal with.
There's going to be this board investigation, an FBI inquiry.
NPR's Kevin Roose, after a close election, Democrats will hold on to the governor's office
in Kansas.
State Senator Cindy Holster has one, according to a race call by the Associated Press.
Zach Boblett with Kansas Public Radio reports.
Despite Kansas having 400,000 more registered Republicans than Democrats, voters decided
to keep a Democrat in the governor's office.
Holster will replace fellow Democrat Laura Kelly, who leaves office in January after
two terms.
Holster ran a populist campaign focused on funding special education, property tax relief,
and a data center moratorium.
She beat a Republican backed early by President Trump.
The Kansas legislature is controlled by Republicans, but they lost seats in the midterms, which
will make it easier for Holster to veto bills.
For NPR News, I'm Zach Boblett in Topeka.
Microsoft got hit with a massive outage across its office software suite today, as NPR's
Kathryn Welch reports.
Thousands of users found themselves unable to access email and messaging.
The outage tracker down detector shows reports suddenly spiked at nearly 130,000 users at
around 1 p.m. Eastern, with thousands more coming in as the day went on.
The outage kept users from accessing email through Outlook or sending message over Teams
and affected other apps in the Microsoft Office suite.
It's not clear what prompted the outage, but in updates on social media, Microsoft said
it was aware that users were encountering issues in "multiple connection methods" in
the Americas.
We should note Microsoft is a financial supporter of NPR.
The company has been providing updates on social media and said it was trying several
fixes.
Kathryn Welch, NPR News.
New York City Mayor Zoran Ramdani says two of the eight people killed yesterday when
an apartment building collapsed in Brooklyn were children.
The three-story building gave way while construction workers were digging at a neighboring lot,
a city official said.
The cause is still under investigation.
Eighteen people were injured in the collapse and rescue operation.
This is NPR News.
Spain's interim lower house of parliament has ratified housing measures designed to
limit evictions and real estate speculation.
The move came a day after a general strike and major street protests over the European
nation's housing cost crunch.
A general election will take place on November 29.
The federal government's new fiscal year is starting out much like the old one, deep in
the red.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the government ran a deficit in the month of October of more
than $400 billion.
Setting aside some calendar quirks, government tax receipts were down 6% in October, compared
to a year ago, while government spending was up by 12%.
Some of that spending increase just reflects a return to normal operations, compared to
October 2025, when the government was shut down.
The Agriculture Department also spent an extra $14 billion last month, with much of that
going to help farmers who were hard hit by the president's trade policies and the high
costs associated with the war with Iran.
In addition, the government paid $115 billion in interest last month, an 11% increase from
October of 2025.
Borrowing costs have been climbing as a result of higher interest rates and the government's
ballooning debt.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
President Secretary Pete Hagseth has awarded a medal to the service member who scolded
him and his staff at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery yesterday.
Specialist Thomas Iglesias reprimanded Hagseth and his staff following a loud laugh during
their photo session at the tomb.
The Pentagon says Iglesias received the Joint Service Commendation Medal, considered to
be one of the higher awards in the military.
I'm Rylan Barton.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
[BLANK_AUDIO]

topics.text: NVIDIA CFO Colette Kress steps in as CEO after Jensen Huang's departure over affair revelations
Kansas Democrat Cindy Holster wins governor's race, AP calls it after close election
Microsoft Office suite suffers major outage affecting Outlook email and Teams messaging
Eight killed as Brooklyn apartment building collapses during neighboring lot excavation
Spain's parliament ratifies housing measures limiting evictions and real estate speculation
US government runs over $400 billion deficit in October as spending rises and receipts fall
Hegseth awards medal to soldier who scolded him at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
